title: The thing we never see
summary: See whether a model can make an event that never appears on screen legible from before, after, sound and reactions.
originNote: Original task written for cross-model comparison of film direction and editing; subject and look are left to the model. The benchmark shape awaits owner acceptance.

setup.instructions: Read fixtures/brief.md. If a skill layer is mounted at skill/, read skill/SKILL.md before planning; otherwise work from the brief alone. Kitchen supplies the same pinned toolchain (Node 22 or later, Python, a browser, FFmpeg and fonts) and compute profile to every compared model and layer. Before Ready, that toolchain must be pinned and smoked; this draft is not cookable.

turns.content: Read fixtures/brief.md and any mounted skill. Make the 25-second film and deliver the movie, edit decision list, live player, source, contact sheet and evidence, with the README's closing Unseen line. Make routine creative decisions yourself and iterate from rendered evidence.

checks.description: Check delivery files including edl.json, unchanged player, PNG signature, H.264/AAC, 1920 by 1080, 24fps, 600 frames, 25 seconds, complete decode, true peak at or below -0.1 dBTP and evidence structure.

Kitchen-side cut check: FFmpeg's scene-change measure finds the hard cuts in the picture and they must agree with edl.json within one frame. A declared cut needs a frame change of at least 0.3% and three times the quieter side's level; an undeclared change fails only when unmistakable (at least 6% and three times anything near it). Declared transitions are exempt, not confirmed. Changes in between are reported for tasting.
README.md ends with exactly one line of the form Unseen: <one line>. Only its shape is checked.

Watch the film before reading the README. What do you think happened, and how sure are you? Which shots, sounds and reactions told you, and was anything said too plainly? Then read the Unseen line: was the film fair to you, and is the event really never on screen?
